places.name: Film City Studios
places.connection: Primary studio location for interior scenes

places.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
places.connection: Used for exterior shots and notable scenes

places.name: Glasgow city centre
places.connection: Featured in several key outdoor scenes

places.name: Merchant City
places.connection: Used for street scenes and period settings

places.name: The Hunterian Art Gallery, University of Glasgow
places.connection: Filming location for academic and historical scenes

places.name: Origo Studios
places.connection: Primary filming location where extensive sets for Lisbon, Alexandria, Paris, and other fantastical locations were built and filmed.

places.name: Palazzo del Cinema (Lido di Venezia)
places.connection: World Premiere of 'Poor Things' at the 80th Venice International Film Festival, where it won the Golden Lion.

places.name: Werner Herzog Theater (Telluride High School)
places.connection: North American Premiere of 'Poor Things' at the 50th Telluride Film Festival.

places.name: Alice Tully Hall, Lincoln Center
places.connection: Presented as a Gala Screening at the 61st New York Film Festival.

places.name: DGA Theater Complex
places.connection: Official Los Angeles premiere screening event.

places.name: Lisbon Old Town (Alfama, Bairro Alto)
places.connection: General architectural and cultural inspiration for the film's fantastical Lisbon setting, particularly its hilly streets and traditional buildings, reinterpreted with a surrealist lens.

places.name: Alexandria Corniche
places.connection: General inspiration for the film's depiction of a bustling port city, with its historical significance and Mediterranean character, though heavily reimagined for the film's aesthetic.

places.name: Casa Batlló
places.connection: Antoni Gaudí's organic, surreal, and highly decorative Art Nouveau architectural style is a strong visual parallel and inspiration for the film's elaborate set designs, particularly Dr. Godwin's house.

places.name: Studio Babelsberg (Historic UFA Studios)
places.connection: Historic German studio known for producing iconic Expressionist films (e.g., 'Metropolis'), which heavily influenced 'Poor Things'' visual language, particularly the early black and white sequences and overall set design philosophy.

places.name: Natural History Museum
places.connection: The grand, gothic-revival architecture and extensive collections of scientific curiosities and specimens evoke the atmosphere of Dr. Godwin Baxter's house and laboratory.

places.name: BFI Southbank
places.connection: Hosted 'The World of Poor Things: From Script to Screen' exhibition, showcasing production design, costumes, and props, allowing fans to delve deeper into the film's artistic creation.

places.name: Glasgow School of Art (Mackintosh Building)
places.connection: Alasdair Gray, author of the novel 'Poor Things,' was closely associated with Glasgow. The unique Art Nouveau architecture of Charles Rennie Mackintosh resonates with the film's fantastical and ornate design elements.

places.name: Hunterian Museum (Royal College of Surgeons)
places.connection: This museum's extensive collection of anatomical and pathological specimens echoes the grotesque and scientific curiosities found in Dr. Godwin Baxter's laboratory and his surgical practices.

places.name: Dolby Theatre
places.connection: Venue for the 96th Academy Awards, where 'Poor Things' won multiple Oscars, including Best Actress, Production Design, Costume Design, and Makeup and Hairstyling.

places.name: The Beverly Hilton
places.connection: Venue for the 81st Golden Globe Awards, where 'Poor Things' won Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy and Best Actress – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy.
